Definition: from G3635; tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome:--grievous, slothful.
BiblicalUsage: Okneros means slothful, tardy, indolent. The lord calls his servant wicked and slothful in Matthew 25:26, and Paul commands in Romans 12:11: not slothful in business, fervent in spirit, serving the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sloth is not rest but rebellion, and the fervent spirit is the cure for it.
